instruction: Press the juicer's knob down until it reaches its pressed position, then let go.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: -0.218 rad is the env's own press target (qmin + 0.25 (qmax - qmin), model 103105; unchanged from v1). New in v2: the knob must be at or beyond it at EVERY step of the 1 s settle phase (worst value over the 20 settle steps), i.e. it must be LEFT pressed, not merely have passed through (E10 J1: pressed, turned back, released was accepted by v1's trace.min). Real world: joint encoder if the appliance is instrumented, otherwise an AprilTag on the knob tracked by a fixed camera for 1 s after the robot stops.

Rationale: the knob must have been moved by the robot: in at least one control step the robot-knob contact impulse ACCUMULATED over all physics substeps of that step is >= 5e-4 N*s (= v1's 0.05 N force floor acting for one 10 ms substep). v1 sampled only the last substep and missed a real jab (E10 J4). Real world: fingertip tactile pads or wrist F/T, integrated over 50 ms, while the fingertip is within 1 cm of the knob.

Rationale: 'then let go' = at every settle step the smallest finger-knob distance (over all substeps) is > 5 mm; 5 mm is the protocol's release gap (well above contact-solver slop of < 0.5 mm, small enough that an opened or withdrawn gripper passes). Together with 'no robot-knob contact impulse in the settle phase' this is the released flag (require_released); the gap is also listed here so that its threshold is part of this file. Real world: finger-to-knob clearance from a calibrated camera / forward kinematics plus zero tactile signal.

source.released_code_predicate: success = juicer_ever_pressed = OR_t(||left TCP - knob mesh centre|| <= 0.14 m); pressed_enough (qpos <= target) computed, unused
source.frozen: 2026-11-12, before any E11 evaluation-set run; thresholds were chosen knowing the E10 report (not blind to it)

notes: Protocol v2. The evaluator runs a 1.0 s settle phase after the policy's last action (robot holds its last command; 20 control steps at 20 Hz); end-state terms (trace.window_*) read only that phase, event terms (trace.count_true) the whole episode. settle 1.0 s (v1 declared 0.5 s, never run): one protocol constant for the three rigid tasks, long enough for the dial to show any spring-back or drift. released = at every settle step: zero robot-knob contact impulse (all links of both arms, accumulated over all substeps) AND finger-knob gap > 5 mm. Knob without a return spring (decision): this contract is written for a LATCHING knob, i.e. one that stays where it is left (the simulated dial has joint stiffness 0, damping 0, friction 0.05; the binding checks stiffness == 0 at reset and stores it in the trace meta). For such a knob 'pressed' is a persistent state, so success = the knob is still at or beyond the pressed position after the robot has let go. A knob WITH a return spring (momentary push button) would spring back on release and could never satisfy this file; it needs a different contract (event form: knob <= target at some step while in robot contact, then released, plus the appliance's own latched state). The route is not constrained: pressing, jabbing or twisting the dial are all accepted if the dial ends pressed and released (E10 J2 interpretation). Not required: which arm, how long the press took.
